synthesis.paragraph: Eight of today's papers carry the tag "Urban Transport and Accessibility", exploring topics such as online-offline feedback networks, active school travel scales in Spain, commercial vehicle load zones in US cities, and active travel policies in England. This same group includes papers on Helsinki's pandemic bicycle lane policies, a methodology for identifying trail deserts, the effects of the Los Angeles Mobility Wallet Program, and dynamic accessibility gaps between urban villages and commercial housing. Outside of this group, one paper develops a GIS-based digital twin framework to assess parcel-level feasibility for Accessory Dwelling Units in Austin, Texas. Another study conducts a systematic literature review to analyze how academic research connects public governance with the creative economy. Finally, a third independent paper uses satellite observations from 2,911 global cities to measure how drought limits the cooling effect of urban vegetation.
